title: ToolRobustBench: Stage-Wise Perturbation Evaluation and Failure Diagnosis for Tool-Calling Agents
summary: ToolRobustBench replaces reliance on clean end-to-end success metrics for tool-calling agents with stage-wise perturbation testing that attributes failures to tool selection, schema grounding, argument binding, and output/runtime handling. Adoption costs benchmark integration effort and additional evaluation compute per model, and the 16 local tools and 14 perturbation subtypes may not cover the reader's production tool surface, requiring custom perturbation design. It can fail as a decision aid if its sampled tools diverge from the deployed stack, since single-family results do not predict mixed-family failure cascades.
rationale: The benchmark is directly usable on a constrained budget via API-based evaluation and addresses a real production gap (localizing tool-call failures), but its diagnostic value for the reader's specific tools and workloads must be validated before being trusted as a release gate.
technique: Stage-wise perturbation benchmark for tool-calling agents
